_comment: Machine-readable rules for what a SKILL.md must contain. Sibling of
report-contract.json: that one defines what a report a writer produces
must contain, this one defines what the skill itself must contain.
Why this exists: lint_skill.py reads these rules rather than hardcoding
patterns. A rule lives in exactly one place; a second copy in the checker
is how this project has had two copies disagree before (see the LINENO
spelling drift in report-contract.json's own history).
The rules are agnix-derived (AS-* for Agent Skills spec, XP-* for
cross-tool compatibility) but reduced to the subset that lint_skill.py
can verify from the SKILL.md file alone, without a network call and
without a provider. agnix's own 702 rules include tool-specific checks
that need the surrounding .claude/, .cursor/, .kiro/ directories; those
are out of scope here and are the ones a separate agnix run covers.
Each rule carries an id, a description and a pattern. Some rules carry
a severity (error or warning): errors gate exit 1, warnings print but
do not gate. Severity exists because a wrong description length is not
the same class of defect as a missing name field; both should be
visible, but only the former should block a release.

frontmatter.name_pattern_why: lowercase, hyphen-separated, alphanumeric. agnix AS-001. An uppercase or underscore name is invisible to some tools.
frontmatter.version_pattern_why: semver so a deployed copy can name itself
frontmatter.description_min_chars_why: agentic tools trigger on this field; under 80 chars rarely fires

trigger_phrases.why: a skill that never says when to trigger is invisible; agnix AS-015

do_not_use.why: the negative trigger is what keeps the skill from firing on unrelated input
